[[:db/retract 17592186184778 :question/answer-fields 17592186183277] {:db/id 17592186184207 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-f6dcfad9-4fa8-567a-ab9a-f61e9f6b1a76" "question-0f199eb7-3af6-57bb-a681-cef6be591a7a"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-f6dcfad9-4fa8-567a-ab9a-f61e9f6b1a76" :question/id #uuid "f6dcfad9-4fa8-567a-ab9a-f61e9f6b1a76" :question/math-academy-id "q-39856" :question/problem "Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$" :question/worked-solution "The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$  

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}x}{‖x‖‖{\text{proj}}_{S}x‖} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 2+0\cdot (-2)+0\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{16}\sqrt{8}} \\  & =\frac{8}{4\cdot 2\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{4},
$$

which is already an acute angle." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-7d5f218f-38ba-531a-af9e-df5b58a66d01"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} 17592186184778 :question/problem "Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 10\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-9{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -9 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=3{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 10\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-4bd4b417-69d9-54a6-aef3-a9bc3d8656f8"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & -6 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.

$$

$$

"question-0f199eb7-3af6-57bb-a681-cef6be591a7a" :question/id #uuid "0f199eb7-3af6-57bb-a681-cef6be591a7a" :question/math-academy-id "q-139476" :question/problem "Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$" :question/worked-solution "The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ -6 & 18\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

{"source" ":org/Math-Academy" "forms" [[:db/retract 17592186184778 :question/answer-fields 17592186183277] {:db/id 17592186184207 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-f6dcfad9-4fa8-567a-ab9a-f61e9f6b1a76" "question-0f199eb7-3af6-57bb-a681-cef6be591a7a"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-f6dcfad9-4fa8-567a-ab9a-f61e9f6b1a76" :question/id #uuid "f6dcfad9-4fa8-567a-ab9a-f61e9f6b1a76" :question/math-academy-id "q-39856" :question/problem "Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$" :question/worked-solution "The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}x}{‖x‖‖{\text{proj}}_{S}x‖} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 2+0\cdot (-2)+0\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{16}\sqrt{8}} \\  & =\frac{8}{4\cdot 2\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{4},
$$

which is already an acute angle." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-7d5f218f-38ba-531a-af9e-df5b58a66d01"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} \n\n$$\n\\Vert \\mathbf{x} - \\textrm{proj}_{S}\\mathbf{x} \\Vert\n$$\n\nas shown in the diagram below.\n\n![](images/d1/d10fd1778529183deb6912cebe9d2b7ad405091fe21a261c464d3d22c6d0860b.png)\n\nLet's find the distance between the vector $\\mathbf{x}$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\\{\\mathbf{a}_1,\\mathbf{a}_2 \\},$ where\n\n![](images/83/83f52159171e736c7ee9edbd0593442d2282572db667eca483e5a77d0b73c9f7.svg)\n\nThe orthogonal projection of $\\mathbf{x}$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by\n\n$$\n\\textrm{proj}_{S} \\: \\mathbf{x} = A(A^T\\!A)^{-1}\\!A^T\\,\\mathbf{x}.\n$$\n\nIn this case, we have \n![](images/9e/9eca38b4b340e44108b073e3f939ce29ae96345b9c1870b9e2cc57a98f9cb077.svg)\nTherefore, we get the following projection: \n\n$$\n\\begin{aligned}{\\text{proj}}_{S}\\,x & =[\\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\\\ 0 & -1 \\\\ -1 & -2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot {([\\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\\\ 2 & -1 & -2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot [\\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\\\ 0 & -1 \\\\ -1 & -2\\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\\cdot [\\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\\\ 2 & -1 & -2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot [\\begin{aligned}0 \\\\ 2 \\\\ 4\\end{aligned}] \\\\  & =[\\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\\\ 0 & -1 \\\\ -1 & -2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot {[\\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\\\ 4 & 9\\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\\cdot [\\begin{aligned}-4 \\\\ -10\\end{aligned}] \\\\  & =[\\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\\\ 0 & -1 \\\\ -1 & -2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot \\frac{1}{2}[\\begin{aligned}9 & -4 \\\\ -4 & 2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot [\\begin{aligned}-4 \\\\ -10\\end{aligned}] \\\\  & =[\\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\\\ 0 & -1 \\\\ -1 & -2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot [\\begin{aligned}2 \\\\ -2\\end{aligned}] \\\\  & =[\\begin{aligned}-2 \\\\ 2 \\\\ 2\\end{aligned}]=\\overset{^}{x}\\end{aligned}\n$$\n\n \n\nFinally, using the distance formula, the distance between $\\mathbf{x}$ and the subspace $S$ is given by\n\n$$\n\\begin{aligned}d(x,\\overset{^}{x}) & =‖x-\\overset{^}{x}‖ \\\\  & =\\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}} \\\\  & =\\sqrt{(0-(-2))^{2}+(2-2)^{2}+(4-2)^{2}} \\\\  & =\\sqrt{4+0+4} \\\\  & =\\sqrt{8} \\\\  & =2\\sqrt{2}.\\end{aligned}\n$$\n\n**Note:** Recall that the vector $\\textbf{x}-\\textrm{proj}_{S}\\,\\mathbf{x},$ whose norm $\\| \\textbf{x}-\\textrm{proj}_{S}\\,\\mathbf{x} \\|$ \\Vert\n$$\n\nas shown in the diagram below.\n\n![](images/d1/d10fd1778529183deb6912cebe9d2b7ad405091fe21a261c464d3d22c6d0860b.png)\n\nLet's find the distance between the vector $\\mathbf{x}$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\\{\\mathbf{a}_1,\\mathbf{a}_2 \\},$ where\n\n![](images/83/83f52159171e736c7ee9edbd0593442d2282572db667eca483e5a77d0b73c9f7.svg)\n\nThe orthogonal projection of $\\mathbf{x}$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by\n\n$$\n\\textrm{proj}_{S} \\: \\mathbf{x} = A(A^T\\!A)^{-1}\\!A^T\\,\\mathbf{x}.\n$$\n\nIn this case, we have \n![](images/9e/9eca38b4b340e44108b073e3f939ce29ae96345b9c1870b9e2cc57a98f9cb077.svg)\nTherefore, we get the following projection: \n\n$$\n\\begin{aligned}{\\text{proj}}_{S}\\,x & =[\\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\\\ 0 & -1 \\\\ -1 & -2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot {([\\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\\\ 2 & -1 & -2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot [\\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\\\ 0 & -1 \\\\ -1 & -2\\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\\cdot [\\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\\\ 2 & -1 & -2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot [\\begin{aligned}0 \\\\ 2 \\\\ 4\\end{aligned}] \\\\  & =[\\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\\\ 0 & -1 \\\\ -1 & -2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot \\frac{1}{2}[\\begin{aligned}9 & -4 \\\\ -4 & 2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot [\\begin{aligned}-4 \\\\ -10\\end{aligned}] \\\\  & =[\\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\\\ 0 & -1 \\\\ -1 & -2\\end{aligned}]\\cdot [\\begin{aligned}2 \\\\ -2\\end{aligned}] \\\\  & =[\\begin{aligned}-2 \\\\ 2 \\\\ 2\\end{aligned}]=\\overset{^}{x}\\end{aligned}\n$$\n\n \n\nFinally, using the distance
